claims.claim: Before starting treatment, EXCLUDE NON-EPILEPTIC CAUSES of seizures such as breath-holding attack, FAINTING, ARRHYTHMIA and pseudoseizures

claims.claim: CLASSIFY THE TYPE OF EPILEPSY on the basis of the description of seizures, neurological examination, EEG findings and neuroimaging
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IDENTIFY AND AVOID PRECIPITANTS if possible -- drugs, SLEEP DEPRIVATION, excess alcohol or alcohol withdrawal
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: START ANTISEIZURE MEDICATION WHEN THE IMPACT OF FURTHER SEIZURES OUTWEIGHS THE RISKS OF TREATMENT
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AFTER ONE SEIZURE ONLY 30 TO 50% OF PEOPLE WILL HAVE A RECURRENCE; factors in deciding to treat include symptomatology (previous seizures may have been unrecognised), signs such as an abnormal EEG or neurological abnormalities, seizure type or epilepsy syndrome, seizure severity, AGE -- elderly people are at higher risk of recurrence -- and the person's wishes
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: LOWEST RECURRENCE RATES are associated with a NORMAL EEG and NO IDENTIFIABLE CAUSE, or when there is a CLEAR AVOIDABLE PRECIPITANT such as sleep deprivation or drugs
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Treatment is usually indicated when 2 OR MORE SEIZURES HAVE OCCURRED WITHIN 6 TO 12 MONTHS -- ABOUT 80% OF PEOPLE WILL HAVE RECURRENT SEIZURES AFTER 2 SEIZURES -- except with a clear avoidable precipitant or with some seizure types such as benign childhood epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SPECIFIC DIAGNOSIS OF SEIZURE TYPE AND, IF POSSIBLE, EPILEPSY SYNDROME ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT FACTORS FOR DRUG SELECTION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For FOCAL (PARTIAL) SEIZURES, AMH's first-line drugs are CARBAMAZEPINE, LAMOTRIGINE and LEVETIRACETAM; second line are clobazam, gabapentin, lacosamide, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pregabalin, tiagabine, topiramate, valproate and zonisamide

claims.claim: For GENERALISED TONIC-CLONIC SEIZURES, first line are LAMOTRIGINE, LEVETIRACETAM and VALPROATE; second line are carbamazepine, clobazam, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin and topiramate
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Table - Choice of antiseizure drug' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For MYOCLONIC SEIZURES, first line is VALPROATE; second line are clobazam, clonazepam, lamotrigine, levetiracetam and phenobarbital -- with LAMOTRIGINE AND LEVETIRACETAM NOTED AS POSSIBLY FIRST LINE IN FEMALES OF CHILD-BEARING POTENTIAL
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Table - Choice of antiseizure drug' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For INFANTILE SPASMS, first line are PREDNISOLONE and TETRACOSACTIDE; second line are vigabatrin, clonazepam and valproate, with VIGABATRIN TO BE USED ONLY IF THERE IS NO SAFER ALTERNATIVE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Table - Choice of antiseizure drug' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: LAMOTRIGINE may be used in adults as monotherapy in focal and generalised seizures and APPEARS TO BE AS EFFECTIVE AS CARBAMAZEPINE, and is also used as adjunctive treatment -- BUT ITS USE IS LIMITED BY THE RISK OF SEVERE ADVERSE REACTIONS SUCH AS STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS

claims.claim: OXCARBAZEPINE is structurally related to carbamazepine and is effective as monotherapy or adjunctive treatment in focal or generalised tonic-clonic seizures; UNLIKE CARBAMAZEPINE IT DOES NOT AUTOINDUCE ITS METABOLISM and has LESS INTERACTION POTENTIAL, so may be an alternative in patients unable to tolerate carbamazepine
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Gabapentin, levetiracetam and topiramate are mainly used as ADJUNCTIVE treatment but may also be used as monotherapy, particularly levetiracetam; lacosamide, pregabalin and zonisamide are used as adjunctive treatment of focal seizures, brivaracetam is also marketed for this, and TIAGABINE IS RARELY USED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PERAMPANEL may be used for adjunctive treatment of refractory focal or generalised tonic-clonic seizures; CANNABIDIOL, FENFLURAMINE, RUFINAMIDE and STIRIPENTOL are used as adjunctive treatments of seizures associated with rarer epilepsies such as Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: VIGABATRIN SHOULD BE USED ONLY WHEN ALL OTHER APPROPRIATE DRUGS HAVE FAILED: IT MAY CAUSE IRREVERSIBLE VISUAL FIELD DEFECTS IN 20 TO 40% OF PATIENTS, and because visual fields are difficult to monitor in young children it should be considered for infantile spasms only where there are no safer alternatives
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ACETAZOLAMIDE and SULTHIAME are approved for epilepsy, but evidence for their clinical efficacy is LIMITED and they are NOT IN COMMON USE IN AUSTRALIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: START TREATMENT WITH ONE FIRST-LINE DRUG ONLY and INCREASE THE DOSE GRADUALLY, ESPECIALLY FOR CARBAMAZEPINE AND LAMOTRIGINE; ABOUT HALF OF ALL PATIENTS ARE SYMPTOM FREE, with manageable adverse effects, ON THE FIRST ANTISEIZURE DRUG TRIED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: BEFORE CHANGING DRUG TREATMENT CHECK THREE THINGS: COMPLIANCE -- noncompliance is a common reason for treatment failure and plasma concentration monitoring can help; DOSE -- ensure the first-line drug is at maximal dose with minimal adverse effects; and DIAGNOSIS -- re-evaluate and confirm it
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: If treatment is still ineffective, ADD an alternative first-line or a second-line drug, and WHEN THE OPTIMAL DOSAGE OF THE SECOND DRUG HAS BEEN ACHIEVED, GRADUALLY DECREASE the dosage of the first
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: EXHAUST ALL REASONABLE OPTIONS FOR MONOTHERAPY before considering long-term treatment with more than one drug; evidence for the most appropriate combinations is lacking, but a reasonable approach is to COMBINE DRUGS WITH DIFFERING MECHANISMS OF ACTION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IN PEOPLE WITH UNCONTROLLED SEIZURES TAKING MORE THAN ONE ANTISEIZURE DRUG, SIMPLIFYING THE REGIMEN MAY IMPROVE SEIZURE CONTROL: AN EFFECTIVE DOSE OF ONE DRUG IS BETTER THAN INEFFECTIVE DOSES OF TWO OR MORE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Treatment withdrawal may be attempted AFTER 2 TO 3 YEARS WITHOUT SEIZURES; good prognostic signs are a history of FEW seizures, ABSENCE SEIZURES ONLY, YOUNGER AGE when control was achieved, NORMAL EEG, NORMAL NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION and ABSENCE OF BRAIN LESIONS

claims.claim: DO NOT STOP ANTISEIZURE TREATMENT ABRUPTLY -- INCREASED SEIZURES AND STATUS EPILEPTICUS MAY OCCUR; reduce the dosage OVER SEVERAL WEEKS TO MONTHS, UP TO 6 MONTHS OR LONGER FOR BENZODIAZEPINES OR BARBITURATES, and WITHDRAW ONE DRUG AT A TIME
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SURGERY may be considered in people with intractable focal epilepsy, and in refractory epilepsy a KETOGENIC DIET may be considered under specialist guidance

claims.claim: SIMPLE FEBRILE SEIZURES -- brief, generalised, occurring only once in 24 hours, with fever from a source outside the CNS -- occur in ABOUT 3% OF CHILDREN aged 6 months to 5 years; there is a 30 TO 50% RISK OF RECURRENT FEBRILE SEIZURES but a LOW RISK OF CHRONIC EPILEPSY and no documented risk of other adverse outcomes
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Acute treatment of a prolonged febrile seizure: DIAZEPAM intravenously or rectally, or MIDAZOLAM intravenously, intramuscularly, intranasally or buccally
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PREVENTION OF FEBRILE SEIZURES IS RARELY NECESSARY; oral or rectal diazepam may be used at the onset of fever in children at high risk of severe or complicated seizures, BUT ITS ADVERSE EFFECTS MAY DELAY DIAGNOSIS OF AN UNDERLYING ILLNESS SUCH AS MENINGITIS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ANTIPYRETICS DO NOT PREVENT FEBRILE SEIZURES, although they may make the child more comfortable; long-term prophylaxis with phenobarbital or valproate is effective but RARELY JUSTIFIED given adverse effects and the usually favourable prognosis, and may be considered only with a history of prolonged seizures or post-ictal hemiparesis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CONSIDER AND DISCUSS THE POSSIBILITY OF PREGNANCY BEFORE SELECTING A SPECIFIC ANTISEIZURE DRUG, and also discuss the risks of unplanned treatment withdrawal

claims.claim: SEVERAL ANTISEIZURE DRUGS -- CARBAMAZEPINE, PHENYTOIN, OXCARBAZEPINE, BARBITURATES, TOPIRAMATE -- INDUCE CYP3A4 AND MAY REDUCE THE CONTRACEPTIVE EFFICACY of combined oral contraceptives, the combined hormonal vaginal ring, oral progestogen-only contraceptives, the etonogestrel implant and ULIPRISTAL
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: USE LEVONORGESTREL IUD, MEDROXYPROGESTERONE DEPOT OR COPPER IUD IF POSSIBLE, as these are unaffected by CYP3A4 inducers; high doses of combined oral contraceptives may be used if these are unsuitable
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CONSIDER WITHDRAWAL OF ANTISEIZURE TREATMENT IN WOMEN PLANNING PREGNANCY WHO HAVE BEEN SEIZURE-FREE FOR AT LEAST 2 YEARS; STOPPING DRUG TREATMENT AFTER THE DIAGNOSIS OF PREGNANCY MAY NOT LOWER THE RISK OF CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The evidence for folic acid reducing neural tube defects in children of women taking antiseizure drugs is LIMITED; however it is recommended to give 5 mg FOLIC ACID DAILY FOR AT LEAST 1 MONTH BEFORE AND 3 MONTHS AFTER CONCEPTION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: THE INCIDENCE OF CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS IN INFANTS OF MOTHERS TREATED WITH ANTISEIZURE DRUGS IS APPROXIMATELY 2 TO 3 TIMES HIGHER THAN IN THE GENERAL POPULATION -- 4 TO 6% VERSUS 2 TO 3%. THE RISK APPEARS HIGHEST WITH VALPROATE AT APPROXIMATELY 10% AND LOWEST WITH LAMOTRIGINE AND LEVETIRACETAM AT APPROXIMATELY 3%
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The risk of a birth defect was thought to increase with the NUMBER of antiseizure drugs taken, but MORE RECENT DATA SUGGEST THE RISK IS RELATED TO THE INDIVIDUAL DRUGS AND THEIR DOSES

claims.claim: PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS OF ANTISEIZURE DRUGS MAY FALL DURING PREGNANCY and compliance may also be a problem; monitor clinically and with plasma concentrations if indicated, PARTICULARLY LAMOTRIGINE, and adjust dosage if necessary
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: HEPATIC ENZYME INDUCERS -- carbamazepine, phenytoin, barbiturates, oxcarbazepine, topiramate -- MAY CAUSE VITAMIN K DEFICIENCY IN THE FETUS, increasing the risk of neonatal bleeding: ENSURE IM VITAMIN K 1 mg IS GIVEN TO THE BABY IMMEDIATELY AFTER BIRTH; antenatal oral vitamin K 10 to 20 mg daily from 36 weeks gestation may be considered, although evidence is inadequate for routine use
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: In STATUS EPILEPTICUS, prolonged and uncontrolled seizures carry a high incidence of serious morbidity and mortality and prompt treatment is required; protocols vary for adults, children and neonates and differ between institutions, so FOLLOW THE LOCAL PROTOCOL IF AVAILABLE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A representative status epilepticus sequence: provide basic life support with oxygen and maintenance of BP and blood glucose; FIRST give a FAST-ACTING BENZODIAZEPINE -- midazolam, diazepam, clonazepam or lorazepam -- with the choice largely depending on whether IV access is available; if seizures continue or to prevent recurrence give a LONG-ACTING antiseizure drug such as IV phenytoin, valproate, phenobarbital or levetiracetam; if status persists give ANAESTHETIC DOSES of thiopental, midazolam or propofol, with assisted ventilation usually required because of the risk of severe respiratory depression
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For ALCOHOL WITHDRAWAL SEIZURES, monitor people at high risk for signs of withdrawal by pulse rate, BP and mental state; BENZODIAZEPINES ARE THE PREFERRED TREATMENT, starting a loading dose regimen at the first signs of withdrawal, and LARGE DOSES MAY BE REQUIRED because of increased hepatic metabolism and CNS tolerance
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: After ACUTE BRAIN INSULT, PROPHYLACTIC ANTISEIZURE DRUG TREATMENT IS NOT INDICATED; drugs used to treat provoked seizures SHOULD BE WITHDRAWN unless unprovoked seizures occur later; and ANTISEIZURE DRUGS ARE NOT INDICATED FOR SEIZURES OCCURRING IMMEDIATELY AFTER A CONCUSSIVE CLOSED HEAD INJURY
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ROUTINE PLASMA CONCENTRATION MONITORING OF ANTISEIZURE DRUGS IS NOT USUALLY USEFUL; it may be used to assess compliance, or for some drugs in special situations such as pregnancy or renal failure
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For phenytoin, carbamazepine and phenobarbital it may be useful to monitor plasma concentrations JUST AFTER A SEIZURE, if dose-dependent adverse effects occur, AFTER A CHANGE IN DOSAGE, or if interacting drugs are started or stopped
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: INTERPRET PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS ACCORDING TO CLINICAL CONDITION: some patients may become seizure free or experience dose-dependent adverse effects at SUBTHERAPEUTIC concentrations, while others will require and tolerate concentrations BEYOND THE THERAPEUTIC RANGE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: An FDA analysis of randomised placebo-controlled trials found an association between some antiseizure drugs and AN INCREASED RISK OF SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIOUR, resulting in a warning in the product information for MOST antiseizure drugs including drugs not in the analysis; THE ASSOCIATION IS CONTROVERSIAL and the benefits will usually outweigh the risks in epilepsy, though the risk-benefit balance MAY BE LESS CERTAIN IN OTHER CONDITIONS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Some adverse effects of antiseizure drugs INCREASE THE RISK OF FRACTURES -- reduced bone mineral density PARTICULARLY WITH BARBITURATES, CARBAMAZEPINE, PHENYTOIN AND VALPROATE, and CNS effects that increase the risk of falling; consider fall prevention strategies and BMD monitoring during long-term treatment, and ensure vitamin D status and calcium intake are adequate
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Epilepsy' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/neurological-drugs/antiseizure-drugs/epilepsy, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
